bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified product portfolio spanning paper, paperboard, corrugated boxes, monocarton and label, animal nutrition and defence electronics, reducing dependence on conventional paper markets
- Integrated manufacturing capabilities across pulp production, paper and paperboard manufacturing; backward integration being advanced through the BCTMP project

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Economic risk - geopolitics, trade dislocation, currency and rates, and low-priced imports — Stated verbatim in the Risk Management table: 'Geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions, inflationary pressures, currency volatility, fluctuating interest rates and a slowdown in domestic demand could adversely affect the Company's operations, input costs, supply-chain stability, export competitiveness and overall financial performance.' Mitigation is a prudent hedging strategy using forward contracts and option structures, continuous forex and interest-rate monitoring, regular engagement with banks, and an optimal mix of fixed and floating rate borrowings. Critically, the Company also 'closely monitors segment-wise import trends and continues to engage with the Government regarding the implementation of Minimum Import Price (MIP) for Writing & Printing paper and Anti-Dumping Duty (ADD) on Packaging Board to address dumping arising from global trade dislocations' - i.e. the Company's margin defence against dumping currently depends on a regulatory remedy it does not control and has not yet obtained. The Board's Report corroborates the exposure: heightened competitive pressure in paperboard from low-cost imports driven by capacity additions in China and Indonesia, limited protection against low-priced imports, and the inverted duty structure under GST 2.0 which caused market ambiguity and lesser buying for two months.
- Demand substitution risk - digitisation eroding paper demand — Stated verbatim: 'Increasing digitisation may reduce demand for paper-based products, which could adversely impact the Company's business performance.' Mitigation is the structural diversification into paperboard, corrugated packaging and animal nutrition to reduce dependence on writing and printing paper, a robust new-product pipeline, distribution strengthening, international markets, and manufacturing flexibility to produce a diverse range of grades. This is the structural risk the entire portfolio shift (paper down to about half of the mix from three-fourths in four years) is designed to answer.
- Raw material risk - wood, pulp, coal and chemical availability — Stated verbatim: 'Shortages of critical raw materials such as wood, pulp, coal and chemicals may adversely affect production capacity and profitability.' This is the risk that actually crystallised in FY 2025-26: the Board's Report states availability of wood continued to be a major challenge, that reduced COVID-period plantation activity caused a sharp rise in wood prices 'severely impacting profitability in FY 2025-26', and that rising demand from adjacent industries such as MDF and plywood raised procurement costs. Mitigation is farm forestry around the manufacturing units, R&D-developed high-yielding pulpwood clones with shorter maturation cycles promoted among farmers, alternative and secondary wood sources and species, and long-term supplier partnerships for other key inputs.
- People risk - attracting and retaining capable workforce — Stated verbatim: 'Failure to attract and retain an efficient and capable workforce may affect the Company's operational efficiency and adversely impact its long-term growth prospects.' Mitigation is a talent management framework identifying critical talent, leadership pipelines, structured succession planning for critical roles to reduce dependency risk, capability building, attrition analysis, engagement initiatives and apprenticeship-led skill development. Supporting BRSR data shows the exposure is live: permanent employee turnover rose to 12.6% in FY 2025-26 from 9.3% in FY 2024-25, with female permanent-employee turnover at 37.1% versus 14.0%, and permanent worker turnover at 6.5% versus 0.3%. 69% of permanent workers are union members (1,128 of 1,629), down from 90% a year earlier, and 5,897 of 7,526 workers are non-permanent - a heavy contract-labour dependence.
- Environmental risk - ESG regulation, climate, carbon, water stress and biodiversity — Stated verbatim: 'Increasing stakeholder expectations, evolving ESG regulations, climate change impacts, carbon emission norms, water stress, biodiversity concerns and sustainability disclosure requirements may affect operations and reputation.' Mitigation is sustainable forestry, renewable energy adoption, energy-efficiency projects, water conservation, circular-economy practices, responsible sourcing and enhanced ESG disclosure aligned with global frameworks; the Company states it has proactively reduced specific water consumption, invested in consumption-efficiency technology and strengthened effluent recycling and treatment, and has commercialised aqueous-barrier coated cupstock board, paper straws and paper carry bags with further plastic-replacement products under development. Note that the BRSR itself is NOT externally assured (assessment/assurance provider stated as 'Not Applicable').
- Regulatory compliance risk - statutory non-compliance, penalties and credit-rating impact — Stated verbatim: 'Non-compliance with statutory regulations may result in penalties and could adversely impact the Company's credit rating.' Mitigation is a comprehensive compliance and monitoring framework backed by a digital compliance management tool tracking all applicable statutory compliances online, plus ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certifications. The rating linkage is the material part: the Company carries an AA/Stable long-term rating, so a compliance failure is framed by management as a cost-of-capital event, not just a fine.
- Project funding and leverage risk - fresh borrowings for the BCTMP pulp mill — The MD&A financial-review narrative states that total debt increased materially during FY 2025-26 'mainly due to fresh borrowings for BCTMP pulp mill project', and that the debt-equity ratio rose year-on-year primarily on account of increased total borrowings, while interest cover fell. This is a structural risk because the BCTMP project - the Company's principal answer to raw-material risk - is being funded with debt into a year in which operating margins declined sharply, and a second large project (the 83 MW hybrid renewable plant for Unit CPM, commissioning Q3 FY 2027-28) is still to be funded. The rupee amounts and ratios behind this statement sit in a leaked financial-review block and have deliberately NOT been reproduced here.
- Occupational health, safety and process-safety risk at manufacturing sites — Not framed as a top-line risk in the risk table, but disclosed at length in BRSR Principle 3 as a managed hazard: the Company cites 'the risks associated with operations and hazardous chemicals used' and runs structured Hazard Assessment / Risk Assessment / Job Safety Analysis, process safety and functional safety procedures, a Safety Committee at each work location, and an ISO 45001:2018 system covering all manufacturing locations and offices, periodically audited by DNV. Reported outcomes for FY 2025-26 are LTIFR of 0.04 for both employees and workers (workers 1.43 in FY 2024-25), with total recordable work-related injuries, fatalities and high-consequence injuries all printed as '-' (STATED NIL) for both employees and workers in both years, and NIL complaints on Working Conditions and Health & Safety.

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells paper and packaging boards including value-added products such as copier, bond, security paper, coated paper and maplitho, along with corrugated boxes and carton boxes. Manufacturing operations span Odisha, Gujarat and Telangana with capabilities across pulp production, paper and paperboard manufacturing, and downstream packaging conversion. outlook.body:
- Structural and progressive portfolio shift towards packaging and downstream conversion businesses, with the paper business coming down to about half from three-fourths over the last 4 years, to increase participation in high-growth and more profitable segments and reduce dependence on conventional paper markets.
- Backward integration through the BCTMP project at Unit CPM to reduce reliance on imported hardwood pulp, improve raw material security and enhance cost efficiency over the medium term.
- Raw-material security through the Social Farm Forestry / farm forestry model - enhancing plantation acreage, developing alternate wood species alongside traditional pulpwood, increasing use of bamboo and veneer waste, exploring captive plantations on degraded wastelands, and maintaining plantation coverage in excess of current fibre requirements.
- Innovation and Reinvention as a core theme - developing differentiated, sustainable fibre-based products (Aqua aqueous-barrier range certified by CPCB, eco-friendly cup stock, premium textured papers, high-strength e-commerce packaging grades, biodegradable barrier-coated boards to replace single-use plastics) and a Centre of Excellence partnership with IIT-Delhi for advanced speciality coatings and food-packaging products.
- Inorganic growth and adjacency expansion - Borkar Packaging to build an integrated packaging ecosystem with a greater footprint in western India and presence in design-led / value-added packaging; Quadragen as entry into the non-antibiotic animal nutraceuticals segment as a complementary growth platform beyond traditional paper markets.
- Corporate structure streamlining via the Scheme of Arrangement (amalgamation of JKPL Utility Packaging Solutions, Securipax Packaging and Horizon Packs into JK Paper; demerger of Enviro Tech Ventures' Demerged Undertaking into PSV Agro Products and amalgamation of the residual ETVL business into JK Paper) to enhance synergies and achieve overall cost reduction.
- Digitalisation as an enabler of operational excellence - PI Vision dashboards, DCS-integrated monitoring systems, analytics-led optimisation tools, improved procurement visibility, and automation of processes to save time/cost and reduce manual intervention; 161 improvement initiatives undertaken in 2025-26.
- Environmental strategy centred on energy optimisation and water stewardship - increasing renewable share of the energy mix (approximately 60% at consolidated level), recycling effluent at source, reducing freshwater intake, reuse of brown sludge in bleaching and white sludges across paper machines, and optimisation of recovery furnace performance.
- Financial strategy of improving liquidity and free cash flows, optimising working capital, maintaining a prudent leverage profile, and reducing financing cost by refinancing high-cost loans with low-cost financing and using government incentives where feasible.
- Brand and channel strategy - strengthening flagship brands (JK Copier, JK Excel Bond, JK Tuff Cote), purpose-driven campaigns (Sandese Aate Hai, Letter to My Supermom and Superdad, AutHer Awards 7th season), and deepening channel partnerships through the JK Jobbers League (over 26% unique participation growth in Season 3) and a revamped Converters Loyalty Programme.
- Balanced talent strategy - nurturing internal capability with selective lateral hiring for specialised and emerging skills, internal job rotations and inter-unit transfers, succession planning and internal promotions, and structured skill-building in digital, automation and data-driven capabilities.
- The stated governance philosophy is 'Maximizing long term shareholders' value' alongside commitment to excellence and customer satisfaction, being a socially valued enterprise and caring for people and environment - framed as observing business practices with the ultimate aim of enhancing long-term shareholders' value while remaining committed to high standards of business ethics. On distribution, the AGM Notice puts before Members as Ordinary Business the declaration of a dividend of Rs 4 per equity share for the financial year ended 31st March 2026. NO Dividend Distribution Policy text was actually delivered: the section carrying that heading contains Board's Report boilerplate instead (significant and material orders, material changes and commitments, conservation of energy, particulars of remuneration, corporate governance), so the Company's stated dividend policy - payout band, frequency, retention criteria - is UNKNOWN from this bundle, not absent from the annual report.
- Renewable energy: approximately 60% of total energy consumption is derived from renewable energy at the consolidated level, and the new BCTMP pulp plant at Unit CPM 'shall be operated entirely on renewable power'.
- Hybrid Renewable Energy Power Plant of approximately 83 MW (solar, wind, energy management/captive power evacuation infrastructure) being set up for Unit CPM expressly for energy security, sustainability, cost reduction and carbon-footprint reduction, expected to be commissioned in Q3 FY 2027-28.
- Forestry and carbon: the Company states it maintains 'plantation coverage in excess of current fibre requirements' as a buffer against climate-related disruption and supply uncertainty, 'while continuing our status as a wood and carbon positive company'. During FY 2025-26 it distributed more than 11.94 crore saplings covering over 90,239 acres, and increased plantation acreage by over 50% in the last three years versus the average of the preceding three years.
- R&D-led forestry: development of high-yielding pulpwood clones with shorter maturation cycles, promoted among farmers, stated to support both farmer livelihoods and long-term raw material security; alternative and secondary wood sources and species being developed alongside traditional pulpwood.
- Water stewardship: technology-led interventions to recycle effluent at source and reduce freshwater intake within processes; reuse of brown sludge in bleaching operations, utilisation of white sludges across paper machines and optimisation of recovery furnace performance, improving recovery efficiency while reducing waste generation and material losses. The Company states it has proactively reduced specific water consumption and strengthened effluent recycling and treatment.
- Plastic replacement / circular economy: commercialised aqueous-barrier coated cupstock board, paper straws and paper carry bags, with further plastic-replacement products under development; biodegradable barrier-coated boards introduced to replace single-use plastics; Aqua brand aqueous-barrier fibre-based products certified by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
- Management-system certifications: ISO 9001:2015 (quality), ISO 14001:2015 (environmental management) and ISO 45001:2018 (occupational health and safety). The ISO 45001:2018 OHS management system covers ALL manufacturing locations and offices and is periodically audited by DNV.
- Safety performance FY 2025-26: LTIFR 0.04 per million person-hours for employees and 0.04 for workers (workers 1.43 in FY 2024-25; employees printed '-' i.e. STATED NIL in FY 2024-25). Total recordable work-related injuries, fatalities, and high-consequence work-related injuries/ill-health all printed '-' (STATED NIL / zero) for both employees and workers in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.
- Safety assurance coverage: 100% of plants and offices assessed for Health and safety practices, and 100% for Working Conditions, during the year. All incidents investigated by a cross-functional team with root-cause analysis, reviewed by Senior Management, with learnings shared across all work locations.
- Value-chain safety assessment is a STATED ZERO, not a gap in the data: the percentage of value chain partners (by value of business) assessed for Health and safety practices and for Working Conditions is printed '-' for both, and the Company states 'Not Applicable as no audit was conducted during FY 2025-26'.
- Employee grievance and complaint outcomes: NIL complaints filed and NIL pending on Working Conditions and on Health & Safety in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25. Structured grievance channels include a Contract Grievance Cell with fortnightly contractor meetings coordinated by the Sr. Manager (IR), a monthly forum headed by the Plant Head, Commercial Head and Plant HR Head, an escalation path to the President & Director if unresolved within a month, and a last-Saturday-of-the-month open session with plant top management.
- Training coverage FY 2025-26: 79% of employees trained on health and safety measures and 73% on skill upgradation; 50% of workers on health and safety and 43% on skill upgradation. Worker coverage fell sharply from FY 2024-25 (99% on health and safety), which the report attributes context to via the note that FY 2025-26 details are post scheme of arrangement.
- Performance and career development reviews: 100% of permanent employees (male and female) received reviews in FY 2025-26, versus 31% of workers (30% male, 79% female).
- Employee welfare: all employees covered under a health insurance / ESI scheme; each manufacturing location has qualified medical staff treating employees, workers and their family members for non-occupational illness, plus ambulance facility; employees and workers covered under a Group Personal Accident Policy and a Benevolent fund in the event of death.
- Transition assistance is a STATED ABSENCE: the Company answers 'No' to whether it provides transition assistance programmes to facilitate continued employability and management of career endings resulting from retirement or termination.
- Freedom of association: 69% of permanent workers (1,128 of 1,629) are members of recognised associations or unions in FY 2025-26, versus 90% in FY 2024-25; 0% of permanent employees are union members in both years (a stated zero).
- Diversity: 2 of 10 Board members are women (20.00%); zero women among the 4 Key Management Personnel (printed '-', a stated nil); women are 6% of total employees and 9% of total workers.
- CSR and community: JK Organisation states it leveraged 27x of the CSR budget invested through government convergence, achieving more than Rs 500 crore in convergence with Government schemes in FY 2025-26. CSR initiatives in livelihood, education, healthcare, environment, women empowerment and skill development benefited over 1.25 million individuals across 17 districts in 10 states, with over 2,000 Self-Help Groups mobilising cumulative savings of about Rs 12 crore and generating monthly turnover of around Rs 44 lakh through women-led enterprises, and assistance to 224 Farmer Interest Groups, 19 Dairy Interest Groups and 22 Village Organisations.
- Stakeholder engagement: identified and mapped internal and external stakeholders with systems to identify, prioritise and address their needs across all plant locations; mechanisms include employee engagement studies, customer satisfaction surveys, supplier and customer plant visits, dealers' meets and lenders' meets, plus a dedicated email id. Employees and Shareholders are both recorded as NOT vulnerable/marginalised groups, engaged 'Regularly'.
- Digital and operational efficiency as an ESG lever: 161 improvement initiatives undertaken during 2025-26; PI Vision dashboards, DCS-integrated monitoring and analytics-led optimisation improving control over critical process parameters.

outlook.body: The single named greenfield project in the routed text is the Hybrid Renewable Energy Power Plant for Unit CPM - comprising Solar, Wind, Energy Management/Captive Power Evacuation Infrastructure or any combination thereof, with an approximate aggregate capacity of 83 MW. The Board's Report states the project is progressing as per schedule and is expected to be commissioned in the third quarter of FY 2027-28, and frames it against a long-term strategy of energy security, sustainability, cost reduction and carbon-footprint reduction. Expansion in FY 2025-26 was otherwise inorganic and structural rather than brownfield: the Company acquired 65.65% of Borkar Packaging Private Limited for cash funded out of internal accruals (subsidiary w.e.f. 28th October 2025), subsequently taken to 71.96% through a private placement of fresh shares - Borkar manufactures folding cartons and corrugated boxes and gives the Company a greater footprint in western India; it raised its stake in Quadragen Vethealth to 65% w.e.f. 22nd August 2025 (additional 2.86%) and in Radhesham Wellpack to 80% w.e.f. 26th September 2025 (additional 20%). The Composite Scheme of Arrangement - amalgamating JKPL Utility Packaging Solutions, Securipax Packaging and Horizon Packs into JK Paper, demerging the Enviro Tech Ventures Demerged Undertaking into PSV Agro Products and amalgamating the residual ETVL business into JK Paper - was sanctioned by NCLT Ahmedabad on 3rd February 2026 and became effective from 15th March 2026, streamlining the corporate structure to enhance synergies and achieve cost reduction. Capacity-side operating commentary is limited to the Packaging Conversion business, which is stated to have increased overall sales volume and plant utilisation with a focus on value-added products and premium customers, and to plantation capacity, where acreage was increased by over 50% in the last three years versus the average of the preceding three years, with 11.94 crore saplings distributed over 90,239 acres in FY 2025-26. NO installed-capacity table and no project cost, capex outlay or funding quantum for the Hybrid Power Project is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.

outlook.body:
- Demand: management states demand across key segments remained stable and domestic demand remained resilient, with strong demand cited in packaging boards, office paper and specialty paper segments.
- Pricing pressure from imports: sustained pressure on realisations driven by increased low-cost imports, particularly in the paperboard segment, following significant capacity additions in Southeast Asian markets such as China and Indonesia; surplus paper and paperboard from those countries exported to India at lower prices, compressing domestic margins.
- Regulatory/duty overhang: limited protection against low-priced imports and the inverted duty structure under GST 2.0, which created ambiguity in the market and lesser buying for two months.
- Wood cost as the dominant input driver: availability of wood continued to be a major challenge; reduced plantation activity during the COVID period adversely affected raw material availability over the past couple of years, causing a sharp rise in wood prices; rising demand from adjacent industries such as MDF and plywood added to procurement costs. Enhanced plantation (acreage up over 50% in the last three years versus the prior three-year average) is expected to improve wood availability and stabilise prices in the coming years.
- Geopolitics and logistics: conflicts in West Asia and the Red Sea resulted in longer shipping routes, higher logistics expenses and delays in the import of pulp, waste paper and chemicals, elevating production costs; energy price volatility and a falling Rupee raise imported-inflation concerns.
- Macro backdrop cited by the CMD: overlapping global polycrises; IMF worst-case scenario of global GDP growth falling to 2% or lower; India entering the phase with robust forex reserves, resilient domestic demand and a diversified industrial base, but exposed as a net energy importer, with risks from rising fertilizer costs, a possible deficient monsoon and early signs of deceleration in purchasing managers' outlook.
- Mix as a margin lever: the Packaging Conversion business performed well with increased overall sales volume and plant utilisation and a focus on more value-added products and premium customers; the shift towards packaging is described as giving greater participation in high-growth and more profitable segments.
- Operating leverage: highest-ever paper and board sales volume of 8.19 lac tons in 2025-26 achieved through scale, market position and execution capabilities despite the adverse pricing environment.
- Structural view on paper demand: in a digital-first world, management argues paper retains a unique place in human expression and its ability to inform, inspire and connect people remains as relevant today as ever.

deepdive.thesis: JK Paper is a vertically integrated paper producer facing margin pressure from soaring wood costs and ASEAN dumping, but is strategically fortifying its position through mechanical pulp self-sufficiency, corrugated acquisitions, and antidumping petitions to capture long-term market share and pricing power.

Realising synergies through the integration of acquired businesses - Borkar Packaging (design-led and value-added packaging, western India footprint) and Quadragen (entry into non-antibiotic animal nutraceuticals) - and completion of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement.

Key business priorities stated: improving operational efficiency and plant utilisation, expanding retail reach across Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets, managing raw material costs through wider sourcing initiatives, and increasing the share of premium and value-added products.

Stated financial strategy of refinancing borrowings at competitive rates, replacing high-cost loans with low-cost financing, maintaining a prudent leverage profile, improving liquidity and free cash flows and optimising working capital efficiency.

Efforts are underway to develop alternate wood raw-material species alongside traditional pulpwood, increase use of bamboo and veneer waste to reduce dependence on wood-based inputs, and explore captive plantations on degraded wastelands.

risks.note: Stated verbatim in the Risk Management table: 'Geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions, inflationary pressures, currency volatility, fluctuating interest rates and a slowdown in domestic demand could adversely affect the Company's operations, input costs, supply-chain stability, export competitiveness and overall financial performance.' Mitigation is a prudent hedging strategy using forward contracts and option structures, continuous forex and interest-rate monitoring, regular engagement with banks, and an optimal mix of fixed and floating rate borrowings. Critically, the Company also 'closely monitors segment-wise import trends and continues to engage with the Government regarding the implementation of Minimum Import Price (MIP) for Writing & Printing paper and Anti-Dumping Duty (ADD) on Packaging Board to address dumping arising from global trade dislocations' - i.e. the Company's margin defence against dumping currently depends on a regulatory remedy it does not control and has not yet obtained. The Board's Report corroborates the exposure: heightened competitive pressure in paperboard from low-cost imports driven by capacity additions in China and Indonesia, limited protection against low-priced imports, and the inverted duty structure under GST 2.0 which caused market ambiguity and lesser buying for two months.
risks.risk: Economic risk - geopolitics, trade dislocation, currency and rates, and low-priced imports

risks.note: Stated verbatim: 'Increasing digitisation may reduce demand for paper-based products, which could adversely impact the Company's business performance.' Mitigation is the structural diversification into paperboard, corrugated packaging and animal nutrition to reduce dependence on writing and printing paper, a robust new-product pipeline, distribution strengthening, international markets, and manufacturing flexibility to produce a diverse range of grades. This is the structural risk the entire portfolio shift (paper down to about half of the mix from three-fourths in four years) is designed to answer.
risks.risk: Demand substitution risk - digitisation eroding paper demand

risks.note: Stated verbatim: 'Shortages of critical raw materials such as wood, pulp, coal and chemicals may adversely affect production capacity and profitability.' This is the risk that actually crystallised in FY 2025-26: the Board's Report states availability of wood continued to be a major challenge, that reduced COVID-period plantation activity caused a sharp rise in wood prices 'severely impacting profitability in FY 2025-26', and that rising demand from adjacent industries such as MDF and plywood raised procurement costs. Mitigation is farm forestry around the manufacturing units, R&D-developed high-yielding pulpwood clones with shorter maturation cycles promoted among farmers, alternative and secondary wood sources and species, and long-term supplier partnerships for other key inputs.
risks.risk: Raw material risk - wood, pulp, coal and chemical availability

risks.note: Stated verbatim: 'Failure to attract and retain an efficient and capable workforce may affect the Company's operational efficiency and adversely impact its long-term growth prospects.' Mitigation is a talent management framework identifying critical talent, leadership pipelines, structured succession planning for critical roles to reduce dependency risk, capability building, attrition analysis, engagement initiatives and apprenticeship-led skill development. Supporting BRSR data shows the exposure is live: permanent employee turnover rose to 12.6% in FY 2025-26 from 9.3% in FY 2024-25, with female permanent-employee turnover at 37.1% versus 14.0%, and permanent worker turnover at 6.5% versus 0.3%. 69% of permanent workers are union members (1,128 of 1,629), down from 90% a year earlier, and 5,897 of 7,526 workers are non-permanent - a heavy contract-labour dependence.
risks.risk: People risk - attracting and retaining capable workforce

risks.note: Stated verbatim: 'Increasing stakeholder expectations, evolving ESG regulations, climate change impacts, carbon emission norms, water stress, biodiversity concerns and sustainability disclosure requirements may affect operations and reputation.' Mitigation is sustainable forestry, renewable energy adoption, energy-efficiency projects, water conservation, circular-economy practices, responsible sourcing and enhanced ESG disclosure aligned with global frameworks; the Company states it has proactively reduced specific water consumption, invested in consumption-efficiency technology and strengthened effluent recycling and treatment, and has commercialised aqueous-barrier coated cupstock board, paper straws and paper carry bags with further plastic-replacement products under development. Note that the BRSR itself is NOT externally assured (assessment/assurance provider stated as 'Not Applicable').
risks.risk: Environmental risk - ESG regulation, climate, carbon, water stress and biodiversity

risks.note: Stated verbatim: 'Non-compliance with statutory regulations may result in penalties and could adversely impact the Company's credit rating.' Mitigation is a comprehensive compliance and monitoring framework backed by a digital compliance management tool tracking all applicable statutory compliances online, plus ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certifications. The rating linkage is the material part: the Company carries an AA/Stable long-term rating, so a compliance failure is framed by management as a cost-of-capital event, not just a fine.
risks.risk: Regulatory compliance risk - statutory non-compliance, penalties and credit-rating impact

risks.note: The MD&A financial-review narrative states that total debt increased materially during FY 2025-26 'mainly due to fresh borrowings for BCTMP pulp mill project', and that the debt-equity ratio rose year-on-year primarily on account of increased total borrowings, while interest cover fell. This is a structural risk because the BCTMP project - the Company's principal answer to raw-material risk - is being funded with debt into a year in which operating margins declined sharply, and a second large project (the 83 MW hybrid renewable plant for Unit CPM, commissioning Q3 FY 2027-28) is still to be funded. The rupee amounts and ratios behind this statement sit in a leaked financial-review block and have deliberately NOT been reproduced here.
risks.risk: Project funding and leverage risk - fresh borrowings for the BCTMP pulp mill

risks.note: Not framed as a top-line risk in the risk table, but disclosed at length in BRSR Principle 3 as a managed hazard: the Company cites 'the risks associated with operations and hazardous chemicals used' and runs structured Hazard Assessment / Risk Assessment / Job Safety Analysis, process safety and functional safety procedures, a Safety Committee at each work location, and an ISO 45001:2018 system covering all manufacturing locations and offices, periodically audited by DNV. Reported outcomes for FY 2025-26 are LTIFR of 0.04 for both employees and workers (workers 1.43 in FY 2024-25), with total recordable work-related injuries, fatalities and high-consequence injuries all printed as '-' (STATED NIL) for both employees and workers in both years, and NIL complaints on Working Conditions and Health & Safety.
risks.risk: Occupational health, safety and process-safety risk at manufacturing sites
